# Log10x POC — local source (file)

_Pulled 8.3K log lines (1.93 MB) across 17 files (tail-sampled; the `window` parameter does not apply to files)._

## Sample composition

These files produced the bytes in the sample. **Confirm this looks like your production mix before trusting the projection** — if 70% of your real-prod bytes come from a service that is NOT in this list, the savings projection is meaningless to you. Widen `paths` or raise `max_pods` (the file cap) if anything looks off.

| File | Bytes | Lines | % of sample |
|---|---|---|---|
| `otel-collector` | 1.17 MB | 3.9K | 60% |
| `frontend` | 0.277 MB | 991 | 14% |
| `kafka` | 0.212 MB | 987 | 11% |
| `cart` | 68.4 KB | 1.1K | 4% |
| `payment` | 36.4 KB | 110 | 2% |
| `accounting` | 35.1 KB | 110 | 2% |
| `shipping` | 30 KB | 170 | 2% |
| `recommendation` | 27 KB | 88 | 1% |
| `astronomy-db` | 18.5 KB | 252 | 1.0% |
| `telemetry-docs` | 18.4 KB | 249 | 1.0% |
| _(7 more)_ | 45.5 KB | — | 2% |

## Projected savings at default rates

_Rates: the vendor's list price where it sells logs per GB, and a per-GB default, marked "default rate", where it bills in other units or publishes no per-GB price. Pass `effective_ingest_per_gb` on `log10x_estimate_savings` or `log10x_savings` once your real $/GB is known to convert these projections into a customer-specific quote._

If your full ingest mix matches this sample, ~77% of your byte volume is non-error high-frequency patterns — candidates for compacting, tiering down or offloading, each of which keeps every line.

**Projected daily ingest** (extrapolated from sample): 46.4 MB.

_File tails carry no time span of their own; the daily projection assumes the sampled bytes cover `1h` (the `window` argument). Pass the window the files actually span to make this projection honest._

_These are list prices and default rates, not predictions of your specific bill: use them to size the order of magnitude, not to negotiate with procurement._

| Log analyzer | Rate | Annual cost | Annual savings |
|---|---|---|---|
| Datadog | $2.50/GB (default rate, a blend of Datadog's two meters, which datadoghq.com/pricing/list gives as $0.10 per GB ingested and $2.50 per million events indexed at 30-day retention, billed annually) | $39 | $30 |
| Splunk | $6.00/GB (default rate, not a Splunk list price) | $95 | $73 |
| CloudWatch Logs | $0.50/GB (ingestion + first-month storage) | $7.9 | $6.1 |
| Azure Monitor | $2.30/GB (Analytics tier ingest, list price) | $36 | $28 |
| Sumo Logic | $2.50/GB (default rate, not a Sumo Logic list price) | $39 | $30 |
| Elasticsearch | $1.00/GB (default rate, an estimate of self-managed infrastructure per GB) | $16 | $12 |
| Coralogix | $1.15/GB (Frequent Search (High) priority, list price) | $18 | $14 |
| Elastic Cloud Serverless | $0.07/GB (Logs Essentials ingest floor; retention billed separately) | $1.1 | $0.85 |
| OpenSearch | $0.10/GB (self-hosted compute baseline (no canonical list rate)) | $1.6 | $1.2 |

## Top patterns in the sample

| # | Identity | Events | % | Bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `$(yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z') info Traces {"resource": {"…` | 1.0K | 14% | 0.316 MB |
| 2 | `$(yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z') info Metrics {"resource": {…` | 889 | 13% | 0.3 MB |
| 3 | `-Ja&Ye|ja9+` | 822 | 12% | 0.256 MB |
| 4 | `$(yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z') info Logs {"resource": {"se…` | 473 | 7% | 0.148 MB |
| 5 | `{"level":$,"time":$(+%s),"pid":$,"hostname":"$","trace_id":…` | 387 | 5% | 0.112 MB |
| 6 | `$(yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z') info Traces {"resource": {"…` | 272 | 4% | 84.6 KB |
| 7 | `::$ - - [$(dd/MMM/yyyy:HH:mm:ss Z)] "GET // HTTP//$1.$1" $ …` | 242 | 3% | 17.9 KB |
| 8 | `$(yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS) $ [$] FATAL: role "root" does no…` | 236 | 3% | 16.2 KB |
| 9 | `info: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore[$] GetCartAsync called…` | 220 | 3% | 26.8 KB |
| 10 | `{"level":$,"time":$(+%s),"pid":$,"hostname":"$","trace_id":…` | 171 | 2% | 47 KB |

_For native stack exclusion configs, paste-ready Receiver YAML, and the full 9-section report, run `log10x_poc_from_siem` once you have credentials available._

## Notes
- wrapped-JSON normalization applied: 8347 of 8347 lines decoded; analysed bytes count the unwrapped payload, raw file size is 3501008 bytes.
